prompt.context: Your client is a national grocery business that manufactures and delivers frozen pizza and ready-to-eat meals. Customers place their orders through a website or over the phone; all phone calls are handled by one call center in the U.S. The company has 400 distribution centers throughout the U.S. It generally takes 2-3 days for orders to arrive once placed. Annual revenue is $1.8 billion. The company has been facing declining sales over the past two years. Sales come primarily from three regions: the Midwest, rural California, and rural Texas — areas where residents do not have easy access to grocery chains.
prompt.question: What should be done to improve sales?

clarifying_info.q: Is the company considering expanding to other regions?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company is not considering expanding to other regions.

clarifying_info.q: Is customer spend consistent across the three regions?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, customer spend is consistent across the three geographical regions.

clarifying_info.q: How many products does the company offer, and what is the price range?
clarifying_info.a: The company has 450 products, with prices ranging from $6 to $20.

clarifying_info.q: Is the sales decline uniform across products?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the decline in sales is uniform across all products.

clarifying_info.q: How do prices compare to traditional grocery stores?
clarifying_info.a: Prices are about 45% of what customers would pay in a typical brick-and-mortar grocery store.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have a loyalty or rewards program?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company does not have a loyalty/rewards program.

exhibits.title: Customer Segmentation Data
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down the customer base into 5 segments by number of customers, number of purchases per year, and average order size.

framework: Diagnose the revenue decline: Revenue = Number of customers x Purchases per year x Average order size
Analyze customer segmentation to identify which levers (customer count, purchase frequency, order size) have the most growth potential
Prioritize segments by revenue contribution and growth opportunity
Develop targeted strategies to increase spend per customer and/or attract new customers
Consider operational and financing constraints for proposed initiatives

questions.prompt: Using the customer segmentation exhibit, calculate annual spend (revenue contribution) for each segment.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply number of customers by purchases per year by average order size for each segment. The key insight is that Segment 2 (800K customers, 20 purchases, $50 avg) is the highest-revenue segment, while Segment 4 (200K customers, 5 purchases, $30 avg) contributes the least.

math.setup: Spend Per Year = # of Customers x # of Purchases Per Year x Avg. Order Size

questions.prompt: Based on the segment data, which segments should the company prioritize for growth and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify segments with the most upside. Segments 4 and 5 have low purchase frequency and/or low order size relative to their customer count, representing the most potential for growth. Segment 3 has the lowest average order size and only moderate purchases. Segments 1 and 2 are already high-value.

questions.prompt: What specific strategies can the company use to increase sales?
questions.guidance: Candidate should articulate strategies tied to the segment findings — increasing purchase frequency and/or order size — and also consider acquiring new customers. Strong candidates will distinguish between website and call center channels and note internet-access constraints in rural areas.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the ways the company can improve sales across its customer base?

categories.name: Increase customer spend per purchase
ideas: Offer discounts or coupons to incentivize larger orders
Use cross-selling (suggest complementary products during checkout)
Bundle products at a slight discount to raise basket size

categories.name: Increase number of purchases per year
ideas: Conduct customer needs assessment to understand reasons for infrequent purchases
Launch targeted promotions to lapsed customers
Follow-up calls from customer service to re-engage customers

categories.name: Increase number of customers
ideas: Marketing and advertising highlighting core competencies: low price and fast delivery
Referral program to leverage existing satisfied customers
Determine customer preferences: delivery speed, taste, product mix
Door-to-door sales in rural areas without internet access
Presence at state fairs and community events to reach customers without internet

categories.name: Operational considerations
ideas: Ensure financing is available for proposed growth initiatives
Acknowledge channel differences: website customers vs. call center customers may require different approaches
Large portion of rural customers may lack internet access — creative outreach needed (door-to-door, events)

recommendation: Focus immediately on Segments 4 and 5, which have the most potential for growth given their low purchase frequency relative to customer count
Launch a loyalty/rewards program and cross-selling features to increase purchase frequency and average order size across all segments
Invest in a referral program and targeted marketing highlighting the company's price advantage (45% of brick-and-mortar) and delivery speed to grow the customer base
risks: Growth initiatives (loyalty program, marketing, referral program) require upfront investment — financing availability must be confirmed
Rural customers without internet access may not be reachable through digital channels, limiting the effectiveness of website-based initiatives
Increasing purchase frequency may strain the 400 distribution centers and call center capacity
next_steps: Conduct a customer needs assessment for Segments 4 and 5 to understand barriers to more frequent purchasing
Model the ROI of a loyalty program and cross-selling feature against implementation costs
Develop a non-digital outreach plan (door-to-door, events) for rural customers without internet access
